headline: Cabinet Division publishes gazette on President Shahabuddin's resignation
summary: Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed will perform the duties of the President until a new one is elected, according to the official notification.
details: The Cabinet Division has officially published a gazette notification regarding the resignation of Mohammed Shahabuddin from the post of President of Bangladesh.
The notification was signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani and follows the president's resignation yesterday afternoon.
According to the gazette, Speaker of the Bangladesh Jatiya Sangsad, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, Bir Bikram, will now perform the duties of the President.
This transition is in accordance with Article 54 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.
Hafiz Uddin Ahmed will serve as the acting president until the next President is elected.
Cabinet Division officials stated that the resignation took effect immediately upon the president signing the resignation letter.
caption:
President Mohammed Shahabuddin has officially resigned. The Cabinet Division has now published the gazette notification.

The Cabinet Division has officially published a gazette notification regarding the resignation of Mohammed Shahabuddin from the post of President of Bangladesh.

The notification was signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani and follows the president's resignation yesterday afternoon.

According to the gazette, Speaker of the Bangladesh Jatiya Sangsad, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, Bir Bikram, will now perform the duties of the President.

This transition is in accordance with Article 54 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

Hafiz Uddin Ahmed will serve as the acting president until the next President is elected.

Cabinet Division officials stated that the resignation took effect immediately upon the president signing the resignation letter.

headline_marked: Tk500 daily wage: [[Tea workers block highway]] in protest
headline: Tk500 daily wage: Tea workers block highway in protest
summary: Workers are demanding a wage increase to 500 Taka per day to cope with rising living costs.
details: Tea workers have staged a blockade on a major highway, bringing traffic to a standstill to demand a higher daily wage.
The protesters are demanding that their daily wage be increased to 500 Taka, citing the need for a better living standard.
The situation remains tense as workers continue their demonstration until their demands are met by the authorities.
Similar protests by tea workers across the region have highlighted ongoing struggles for fair compensation and land rights.
caption:
Tk500 per day. That's the demand of tea workers who have now blocked a highway in protest.

Tea workers have staged a blockade on a major highway, bringing traffic to a standstill to demand a higher daily wage.

The protesters are demanding that their daily wage be increased to 500 Taka, citing the need for a better living standard.

The situation remains tense as workers continue their demonstration until their demands are met by the authorities.

Similar protests by tea workers across the region have highlighted ongoing struggles for fair compensation and land rights.
